title: Modules: reusable tools
subtitle: Put reusable functions in a separate file and import them from another file.
concept: Put reusable functions in a separate file and import them from another file.
intuition: Keep familiar tools in a toolbox and retrieve them by name.

body.title: Use a built-in Python module
body.text: import math loads Python's built-in math module, a collection of related tools. math.sqrt(9) calls its square-root function and returns 3.0. The dot joins the module name to the tool name. You do not need to implement the square-root algorithm.

body.title: Put your tools in helpers.py
body.text: The appendix defines double in helpers.py. After from helpers import double, main.py can call double(5). Save the files in one directory, enter it in a terminal, and run main.py. Do not name your own file math.py or json.py: it can hide the standard module.

body.title: Keep demonstrations out of imports
body.text: Ordinary top-level statements also execute the first time a module is imported. To avoid prompting the user during an import, put demonstrations and command-line operations under if __name__ == "__main__":. Treat this as an entry-point guard: it runs when the file is executed directly, not when imported. You need not study the double underscores yet.

formalDefinition.text: import makes module tools available. An entry-point guard runs a demonstration only when the file is executed directly.
conditions: Save helpers.py and main.py in the same directory for the two-file example.
This lesson gives sqrt nonnegative inputs.

commonMistakes.claim: Importing a file never runs its top-level statements.
commonMistakes.correction: Ordinary top-level statements execute too. Put demonstrations inside the entry-point guard.

commonMistakes.claim: My math.py cannot affect import math.
commonMistakes.correction: A local file with the same name can hide the standard module. Choose a different filename.

learningCheck.question: Where should demonstration code go in a module intended for import?
choices: At the top level, prompting on import
In a comment, which will execute too
learningCheck.explanation: The guard groups the demonstration steps that should run only when the file is executed directly.
feedback: Top-level statements run on import and may interrupt the caller.
